natural: to retaliate out of a grudge

meaning.en: To take revenge on someone because of a personal grudge.
meaning.zh: 因为心里怀有私怨而对人进行报复。

equivalents: get back at someone out of spite

examples.zh: 他因为被批评过，就挟嫌报复，故意在报销上刁难同事。
examples.en: Because he had been criticised, he got back at his colleague out of spite by making his expense claims difficult.

examples.zh: 警方认定这起纵火案是挟嫌报复。
examples.en: The police concluded that the arson was an act of revenge over a grudge.

usage.en: Usually used of a specific incident, in news and legal reports. Predicate.
usage.zh: 多指具体事件，常见于新闻和法律文书。作谓语。

meaning.en: To put someone in a post he is not suited for; to appoint the wrong person.

equivalents: the wrong man for the job
a square peg in a round hole

examples.zh: 项目接连出问题，根子就在用非其人。
examples.en: The project kept running into trouble, and the root cause was putting the wrong person in charge.

examples.zh: 用人要看长处，否则只会用非其人。
examples.en: Staff should be chosen for their strengths; otherwise you simply end up with the wrong people in the wrong jobs.

usage.en: Used when criticising an appointment or a manager's judgement. Predicate, formal.
usage.zh: 多用于批评任用或管理上的失误。作谓语，偏书面。

natural: an illness of the heart and belly

meaning.en: A grave, deep-seated trouble close to the vital core, one that is hard to cure and fatal if ignored.
meaning.zh: 比喻长在要害处、难以根治的严重祸患。

examples.zh: 内部腐败才是这家企业的腹心之疾。
examples.en: Internal corruption was the real mortal threat to the company.

examples.zh: 他把贫富悬殊看作社会的腹心之疾。
examples.en: He regarded the wealth gap as a deep-seated sickness of society.

usage.en: Used of threats from within or at the centre, in contrast with 癣疥之疾 (minor ailments). Formal; object or predicate.
usage.zh: 多指内部或要害处的重大祸患，常与“癣疥之疾”对比。书面语，作宾语、谓语。

natural: coming from the depths of one's heart

meaning.en: Said of words or feelings that are completely sincere and come from the bottom of one's heart.
meaning.zh: 指话语或感情是真心实意的，出自内心深处。

equivalents: from the bottom of one's heart

examples.zh: 这些感谢的话，句句发自肺腑。
examples.en: Every word of thanks was heartfelt.

examples.zh: 他发自肺腑的演讲打动了在场所有人。
examples.en: His speech, which came straight from the heart, moved everyone present.

usage.en: Usually describes words, feelings or thanks. Predicate or attributive (发自肺腑的话).
usage.zh: 多形容话语、感情、谢意。作谓语、定语（发自肺腑的话）。

natural: to ruin the people and harm all creatures

meaning.en: To oppress the people and damage the common good, said of tyrannical rulers or of ruthless exploitation.
meaning.zh: 残害百姓，危害万物，多指暴政或肆无忌惮的掠夺。

examples.zh: 贪官污吏残民害物，激起了百姓的怨恨。
examples.en: Corrupt officials bled the people dry and stirred up deep resentment.

examples.zh: 竭泽而渔式的开发只会残民害物。
examples.en: Development that drains everything for short-term gain only harms people and nature.

usage.en: A strong condemnation, mostly of rulers or officials; formal.
usage.zh: 谴责意味强，多指统治者或官吏。书面语。

natural: to shut the door once the thief has gone

meaning.en: To take precautions only after the loss has happened, when it is too late.
meaning.zh: 东西被偷走以后才想起关门，比喻事后才采取措施，为时已晚。

equivalents: lock the stable door after the horse has bolted

examples.zh: 等数据泄露了才加强防护，这不是贼走关门吗？
examples.en: Tightening security only after the data has leaked is shutting the door once the thief has gone.

examples.zh: 事故发生后才检修设备，未免贼走关门。
examples.en: Only repairing the equipment after the accident is rather too late.

usage.en: Criticises belated action. Casual; predicate. Also said 贼去关门 or 贼去了才关门.
usage.zh: 批评事后才补救。口语，作谓语。也说“贼去关门”“贼去了才关门”。

meaning.en: An arrangement that suits both parties, so that each gets what is convenient for him.
meaning.zh: 对双方都方便、都有好处。

examples.zh: 你顺路捎我一程，咱们两得其便。
examples.en: If you give me a lift on your way, it suits us both.

examples.zh: 两校共用实验室，两得其便。
examples.en: The two schools share a laboratory, which suits both of them.

usage.en: Often used in the pattern ……，两得其便. Predicate; formal or semi-formal. Read 便 as biàn.
usage.zh: 常说“……，两得其便”。作谓语，偏书面。“便”读 biàn。

natural: to hold a view with good grounds

meaning.en: Of an opinion or argument: based on solid reasons and evidence, not made up.
meaning.zh: 指看法、主张有根据、有道理。

examples.zh: 他的批评持之有故，大家不得不认真考虑。
examples.en: His criticism was well-founded, so everyone had to consider it seriously.

examples.zh: 论文的观点持之有故，言之成理。
examples.en: The paper's views are well grounded and make sense.

story.en: In criticising rival schools, Xunzi grants that their views 'have grounds and their words make sense' (持之有故，言之成理), yet are enough to mislead the foolish.
story.zh: 荀子批评诸家之说，说他们“然而其持之有故，其言之成理，足以欺惑愚众”。

usage.en: Usually paired with 言之成理: 持之有故，言之成理. Predicate; formal.
usage.zh: 常与“言之成理”连用：持之有故，言之成理。作谓语，书面语。

meaning.en: To attack without a formal declaration of war; by extension, to start a fight or campaign without warning.
meaning.zh: 没有正式宣战就发动进攻；也比喻事先不打招呼就开始行动或竞争。

examples.zh: 敌军不宣而战，突然越过了边界。
examples.en: The enemy crossed the border suddenly, without any declaration of war.

examples.zh: 对手不宣而战，一夜之间在全国大幅降价。
examples.en: Our rival launched a price war without warning, slashing prices nationwide overnight.

usage.en: Literal in military contexts, figurative in business and sport. Predicate.
usage.zh: 军事上指字面意思，商业、体育中多为比喻。作谓语。

meaning.en: Too appalling or too pitiful to bear looking at.
meaning.zh: 景象太凄惨或太糟糕，让人不忍心看。

equivalents: a sight too awful to behold

examples.zh: 地震后的废墟目不忍睹。
examples.en: The ruins left by the earthquake were too terrible to look at.

examples.zh: 这场比赛输得目不忍睹。
examples.en: The way we lost the match was painful to watch.

usage.en: Used for disasters and also, loosely, for very poor performances. Also written 目不忍视. Predicate or complement.
usage.zh: 可用于灾难场面，也可泛指表现极差。也作“目不忍视”。作谓语、补语。

meaning.en: To mistake something sickeningly affected or fawning for something charming or funny.
meaning.zh: 把令人恶心的矫揉造作或谄媚当作有趣、动人。

equivalents: think one's own cringe is cute

examples.zh: 他把低俗的恭维当幽默，真是肉麻当有趣。
examples.en: He takes his crude flattery for wit, mistaking cringe for charm.

examples.zh: 别肉麻当有趣了，没人觉得这样的玩笑好笑。
examples.en: Stop thinking your cringeworthy jokes are funny; nobody laughs.

usage.en: A sarcastic put-down, written 肉麻当有趣 in full. Casual; predicate.
usage.zh: 带讽刺意味的批评，口语。作谓语。

synonyms: 猪头挂在花椒树上——肉麻

literal: meet · calamity · turn into · good fortune

meaning.en: To meet with trouble and have it turn out well; often used as a good wish.
meaning.zh: 遇到灾难而化为吉祥，常用作祝福语。

examples.zh: 愿你此行遇难成祥，一路平安。
examples.en: May your trip be safe, and may any trouble turn into good fortune.

examples.zh: 这次虽有风险，但大家相信他会遇难成祥。
examples.en: There is risk this time, but everyone believes he will come through it well.

usage.en: Often paired with 逢凶化吉: 逢凶化吉，遇难成祥. Used as a blessing; formal.
usage.zh: 常与“逢凶化吉”连用：逢凶化吉，遇难成祥。多作祝福语，书面语。

natural: to accept everything on the list

meaning.en: To accept everything offered or demanded without picking and choosing, often without thinking critically.
meaning.zh: 按照清单全部接受，指对别人给的或要求的一概接受，不加挑选。

examples.zh: 网上的各种说法不能照单全收。
examples.en: You can't just accept everything people say online.

examples.zh: 老板提出的要求，他全都照单全收。
examples.en: Whatever demands the boss made, he accepted them all.

usage.en: Can be neutral or mildly critical, depending on whether the acceptance is uncritical. Predicate.
usage.zh: 是否含贬义要看接受得是否盲目。作谓语。

pinyin: hóng huā hái děi lǜ yè fú
literal: red · flower · still · must · green · leaf · support
natural: even a red flower needs green leaves to set it off

meaning.en: Even a talented or outstanding person needs the support of others in order to shine.
meaning.zh: 再出色的人也需要别人的帮助和衬托。

equivalents: even stars need a supporting cast

examples.zh: 红花还得绿叶扶，你再能干，也离不开团队。
examples.en: Even the most capable person needs help; you can't do without the team.

examples.zh: 他总说红花还得绿叶扶，把成绩归功于同事。
examples.en: He always says even the star needs the supporting cast, and credits his colleagues.

usage.en: Used to encourage cooperation or to be modest. Note 得 is read děi. Casual; often a full sentence.
usage.zh: 用于强调合作或表示谦虚。“得”读 děi。口语，常单独成句。

synonyms: 牡丹虽好，全仗绿叶扶持

pinyin: chī xián luó bo dàn cāo xīn
natural: eating salty radish and worrying blandly

meaning.en: To worry needlessly about things that are none of one's business.
meaning.zh: 比喻替别人操不必要的心，管与自己无关的事。

examples.zh: 人家夫妻的事，你吃咸萝卜淡操心干什么？
examples.en: Why worry about what's going on between that couple? It's none of your business.

examples.zh: 别吃咸萝卜淡操心了，先管好你自己的功课。
examples.en: Stop fussing over other people and take care of your own homework first.

usage.en: A casual, slightly teasing rebuke. Predicate.
usage.zh: 口语，带调侃，多用于劝人别瞎操心。作谓语。

pinyin: qǐng kè róng yì sòng kè nán
literal: invite · guest · easy · see off · guest · hard
natural: inviting guests is easy, seeing them out is hard

meaning.en: Starting something is easy, but finishing or getting out of it gracefully is hard.
meaning.zh: 请客人来容易，要让客人离开却难，比喻事情开头容易，收场难。

equivalents: it is easy to start but hard to end

examples.zh: 请客容易送客难，这个项目一旦启动就不好收场。
examples.en: Easy to start, hard to end: once this project is under way it will be hard to wind up.

examples.zh: 请客容易送客难，他又被那几位老朋友拖到半夜。
examples.en: It's easier to invite guests than to get them to leave; those old friends kept him up until midnight.

usage.en: Often used with humour in invitations and in business. Casual; often a full sentence.
usage.zh: 常带诙谐，用于请客或做事开头容易收场难时。口语，常单独成句。

pinyin: zhàn xiǎo pián yi chī dà kuī
literal: grab · small · advantage · suffer · big · loss
natural: grab a small gain and suffer a big loss

meaning.en: Greedily grabbing a small advantage will end up costing you much more.
meaning.zh: 贪图小利，最后会吃大的亏。

equivalents: a small gain, a big loss

examples.zh: 他为了赠品买了一堆没用的东西，真是占小便宜吃大亏。
examples.en: He bought a pile of useless things for the freebies; a small gain that cost him dearly.

examples.zh: 老人们常告诫我们，占小便宜吃大亏。
examples.en: The elders often warn us that grabbing small gains leads to big losses.

usage.en: A common warning, often about scams and bargains. Note 便宜 is read pián yi. Casual.
usage.zh: 常用于提醒人别贪小便宜上当。“便宜”读 pián yi。口语。

pinyin: zǒu yī bù suàn yī bù
literal: walk · one · step · count · one · step
natural: take one step and count it as one step

meaning.en: To deal with things as they come, without a long-term plan.
meaning.zh: 不作长远打算，遇到什么情况再处理什么情况。

examples.zh: 毕业以后的事，我还没想好，走一步算一步吧。
examples.en: I haven't decided what to do after graduation; I'll take it as it comes.

examples.zh: 创业初期没有计划，只能走一步算一步。
examples.en: In the early days of the start-up we had no plan and could only play it by ear.

usage.en: Can sound resigned or carefree; neutral to mildly negative. Often a clause on its own. Also said 走一步看一步.
usage.zh: 可显得无奈或洒脱，中性偏贬。常单独成句。也说“走一步看一步”。

synonyms: 脚踩西瓜皮——滑到哪里算哪里
